title: The Riemann curvature tensor
summary: Higher covariant derivatives (Definition 8.1); the curvature operator R(X,Y)Z = ∇_X∇_Y Z − ∇_Y∇_X Z − ∇_[X,Y] Z as a tensor (Theorem 8.9) and its symmetries including the first Bianchi identity; sectional curvature on 2-planes (Definition 8.14) and its coordinate expression; Ricci and scalar curvature; constant curvature and the form of R (Theorem 8.29); flat manifolds; curvature of spheres, hyperbolic space and Lie groups.

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is Gudmundsson chapter 8 (Definitions 8.1, 8.14, 8.27; Theorems 8.9, 8.29; Examples 8.17–8.18, 8.23) with Sternberg §3.7 and §3.11–3.13, Wendl §6.1 and Lee chapter 7 as the commercial reference.

preparation.description: Read Gudmundsson chapter 8, pp. 109–112: Definition 8.1 (covariant derivatives of tensor fields), Theorem 8.9 (the curvature operator is tensorial) and Proposition 8.10 (symmetries).
Read pp. 113–114: Definition 8.14 (sectional curvature), Example 8.17 (coordinate expression), Example 8.18 (Euclidean space is flat).
Read pp. 118–120: Definition 8.27 (the tensor of constant curvature), Lemma 8.28 and Theorem 8.29.
Open-licensed alternatives: Sternberg §3.7 (curvature), §3.11–3.13 (curvature identities, sectional and Ricci curvature); Wendl §6.1 (locally flat manifolds).
